overview: Surah Al-Falaq (The Daybreak) is the 113th chapter of the Holy Quran, consisting of 5 verses in Juz 30. Together with Surah An-Nas (114), it is known as Al-Mu'awwidhatayn—the two surahs of seeking refuge in Allah.

The surah teaches believers to turn directly to the Lord of the daybreak—the One Who splits the darkness of night with dawn—for protection from external harms: the harm of created beings, the darkness of night as it settles, those who practice sorcery, and the envy of an envier when they act upon it.

By placing Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas at the very end of the Quran, the scripture closes on a note of humble reliance on Allah alone for safety and peace of mind. Muslims commonly recite it in daily prayers, after obligatory salah, and before sleeping.
mainThemes: Seeking refuge exclusively in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.
Protection from external harms: creation, darkness, sorcery, and active envy.
Reliance on Allah rather than fear or superstition.

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ told Uqbah ibn Amir about Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas: 'No seeker of refuge can seek refuge with anything like these two.'
The Prophet ﷺ used to recite Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Al-Falaq, and Surah An-Nas every night before sleeping, blowing into his cupped hands and wiping over his body three times.

faqs.question: How many verses are in Surah Al-Falaq?
faqs.answer: Surah Al-Falaq has 5 verses (ayahs) and is the second-to-last chapter of the Quran in Juz 30.

faqs.question: What does Al-Falaq mean?
faqs.answer: Al-Falaq means 'The Daybreak' or 'The Dawn,' referring to Allah splitting open the darkness with morning light.

faqs.question: What are Al-Mu'awwidhatayn?
faqs.answer: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn refers to Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah An-Nas (114), the two closing surahs in which believers seek refuge in Allah.

faqs.question: When is Surah Al-Falaq recited?
faqs.answer: Following prophetic practice, Surah Al-Falaq is recited alongside Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah An-Nas before sleep (Sahih al-Bukhari 5017), in daily prayers, and in morning and evening remembrances.

relatedSurahs.reason: Surah An-Nas pairs with Al-Falaq as Al-Mu'awwidhatayn.
Surah Al-Ikhlas completes the three closing Quls.
Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Quran just as Al-Falaq and An-Nas close it.
